title: You're not gonna make it
summary: A deliberately harsh 'real negativity' list of reasons viewers will not make it: waiting for perfect conditions, blaming external factors, needing encouragement, an external locus of control, blaming genetics, using past inaction as an excuse, entitlement and the blackpill. NH argues responsibility, willpower, gratitude and an internal locus of control are the only way out.
claims: Waiting for perfect conditions or a perfect plan before trying is laziness disguised as perfectionism; the perfect plan is the one you put into action
Rain, homework, poor sleep or work hours are excuses; you created the circumstances, often by procrastinating, and telling others only soothes your own disappointment
At 16 he woke at 5 am daily to sprint in the park before school regardless of rain or snow, and ran in the mountains in bad weather
Willpower is trainable: each time you push through you teach yourself to win, each time you quit for a bad reason you reinforce weakness
It is not always your fault, but it is always your responsibility
He sticks to training because his goal never ends, so he never quits
Relying on others for motivation is like a fire you must feed with outside wood; the motivation must come from inside you
He watched countless gym newcomers who only trained while he babied them and disappeared once he did not
Most gains are achieved alone; if you need a crew or commercial gym to train, your motivation is fragile, as shown by people who stopped training during the pandemic lockdowns
Decide once that you will train for the rest of your life regardless of external factors
No one, including him, can lift the weights for you; programs and advice are useless if you do not act
Become your own saviour: picture the child you were and become the adult that child needed
Locus of control is a learned belief, not innate, so you can switch from external to internal
Even if fate existed, believing in free will and responsibility leads to better lives; blackpilled people believe in determinism and give up
Being told you have bad genetics feels good because it excuses a poor physique; real honesty is saying you do not train hard, are not consistent and not patient
Two clones with identical genetics, one told he has good genetics and one bad, would end up with different physiques in 10 years via self-fulfilling prophecy (Pygmalion effect)
It is never too late to start lifting, even at 80; using past inaction as an excuse is a reverse sunk-cost fallacy
If you have two working arms and two working legs you have everything needed to lift; complaining about genetics insults those born without them
His mother would make him look at his roof, bed and moving limbs to show he had everything needed to get up and become someone
Practise gratitude: focus on what you can influence rather than what you lack
Life is like poker: good players play the hand they were dealt as well as they can instead of complaining about variance
Entitlement breeds envy; when someone has what you want, learn how they got it instead of assuming they cheated or got lucky
The blackpill is not brutal honesty but an extra illusion that always blames things outside your control so you can feel better and do nothing
Real negativity that makes you uncomfortable and pushes you to act is useful; fake negativity keeps you static
Take advice from lions, not from people who have given up
